div.head: IV Eg 13
div.ab: ⁊ ic wille, þæt tunesmen ⁊ heora hyrdas habban þás ylcan smeagunge on minum cucum orfe ⁊ on minra þegena, ealswa hy habbað on heora ágenum.
⁊ ic wille, þæt tunesmen ⁊ heora hyrdas habban þas ylcan smeagunge on minum cucum orfe ⁊ on minra þegena, ealswa hy habbað on heora agenum.
Ruricolis quoque ipsis hanc eandem statuo rectitudinem, ut in meis meorumque principum pecoribus et pascuis habeant exquisitionem.
⁊ ic wille þæt tunesmen ⁊ heora hyrdas habban þas ylcan smeagunge on minum cucum orfe ⁊ on minra þegena, ealswa hy habbað on heora agenum.

Und ich will, dass die Dorfbauern und deren Hirten diese selbe Untersuchung [zu üben das Recht] haben an meinem und an meiner Thegnas lebendem Vieh [der Gutsdomäne], wie sie [es] an ihrem eigenen haben.
And I will that the villagers and their herdsmen have [the right to make] this same inquiry concerning my live cattle and my thegns' [on the demesne], just as they have concerning their own.
And it is my will that villagers and their herdsmen shall have the same right of investigation with regard to my livestock and that of my thegns as they have with regard to their own.
And it is my will that villagers and their herdsmen may hold the same investigation among my livestock and among that of my thegns, as they hold among their own.

note.seg: Vgl. o. 8f.; Gl Gemeinheit 10; die Domäne des Herrschaftsguts (s. d. Gl 1a) unterliegt also denselben Kautelen des Handels (s. d. Gl 8) wie der Bauer (s. d. Gl 13f.). Doch waren Herr und Vogt regelmässig selbst Kaufzeugen, also die Formalitäten für sie leichter

Cf. above 8f.; Gl Gemeinheit 10; the demesne of the manor (see that word in Gl 1a) is thus subject to the same safeguards in trade (see that word in Gl 8) as the peasant (see that word in Gl 13f.). The lord and the reeve, however, were regularly themselves witnesses to purchases, so that the formalities were easier for them
Auch Cnut 1027, 12 mahnt, nicht etwa zugunsten königlicher Finanz Polizei und Recht zu verletzen
Cnut 1027, 12 too admonishes that public order and justice must not be violated, say, for the benefit of the royal finances
